label: late original inputs and <DEL> in sequences that begin with c/l/2/3/w/k/q/o/v
explanation: Fires only during reading: original positions t>=3 and the <DEL> step (27% of <DEL> steps, about 48% of activation mass). It is almost silent in the copy phase (0.6% of mass) and never fires at t<=2. Whether it fires depends on which tokens opened the sequence. It is strongest when the first (and early) originals come from {c,l,2}, followed by {3,w,k,q,o,v}; the rate for first_tok=c is 3.9x baseline. The top activations are <DEL> steps in sequences starting with two or more c/l/2 tokens. The current input also modulates it: j,r,u,g,f,s increase it and repeated tokens (in_first=0) suppress it. Rate rises with orig_idx and is highest at <DEL>. It looks like a graded readout of the early-prefix identity rather than a clean boolean: the predicate gets about 0.81 mass recall but only about 0.40 precision. Many sequences opening with these tokens never fire, and some sequences with these tokens at position 1-2 rather than 0 do fire.
